question.prompt: A rectangular floor that is \(10\) feet wide and \(17\) feet long is tiled with \(170\) one-foot square tiles. A bug walks from one corner to the opposite corner in a straight line. Including the first and the last tile, how many tiles does the bug visit?

solutions.title: Count entries into new tiles
solutions.explanation:
Each time the bug crosses an interior grid line, it enters another tile, unless it crosses a horizontal and vertical line simultaneously at a tile corner. We first rule out that possibility.

Place the starting corner at \((0,0)\) and the opposite corner at \((17,10)\). The diagonal satisfies
\[
17y=10x.
\]
At a tile corner, both coordinates are integers. Since \(10\) and \(17\) are relatively prime, this equation forces \(x\) to be a multiple of \(17\). There is no such integer with \(0<x<17\), so the diagonal passes through no interior tile corner.

The bug crosses each of the \(16\) interior vertical grid lines and each of the \(9\) interior horizontal grid lines exactly once. These are \(16+9=25\) separate crossings. Each enters a new tile, and the straight path never returns to an earlier tile.

Including the starting tile, the total is
\[
1+16+9=\boxed{26}.
\]
The answer is choice \(\text{C}\).
